voiceover: Does the Koran confirm the very Scriptures it contradicts? The Koran calls itself musaddiq — the confirmer of the Scriptures that came before it. It affirms the Torah given to Moses and the Gospel given to Jesus as true revelation from God — 'confirming what was before it.' It even tells Christians to judge by their own book: 'let the People of the Gospel judge by what Allah has revealed therein.' And it commands the Prophet himself: if you are in doubt, ask those who have been reading the Scripture before you. So the Koran sends everyone back to the Torah and the Gospel as a trustworthy standard from God. But that Gospel — the one Christians actually held — teaches what Islam denies. It says Jesus was crucified, and that he is the divine Son of God. The Koran denies both. So the Koran points to, and confirms, the very books that contradict it. And the tension comes from the Koran's own words. Is there a way out of it? That's the question at the heart of Christopher Frost's book, The Islamic Dilemma. Read it together, chapter by chapter, in our reading club.
